EC1: - Women [AND] who are considered high-risk based on a greater than 25% lifetime risk of breast cancer as per the IBIS (International Breast Cancer Intervention Study) Breast Cancer Risk Evaluation Tool
EC2: - Pathology that is felt to be discordant with imaging
EC3: - Extensive calcifications extending more than 20 mm [OR] and/or masses greater than 30 mm
EC4: - The following lesions will be [NOT] excluded based on their increased risk of upstaging; lesions (other than fibroadenomas, [OR] phyllodes [OR] and papillomas) that are associated with a palpable mass, [OR] ADH (atypical ductal hyperplasia) [AND] with high-risk features (ADH [AND] with zonal necrosis, significant cytological atypia [OR] or more than 2 foci), LCIS (lobular carcinoma in situ) [AND] with high-risk features (associated with ADH, [OR] pleomorphic LCIS, [OR] zonal necrosis [OR] and > 4 foci) [OR] or discordant with imaging, [OR] papilloma with atypia, [OR] and spindle cell lesion (especially if there is atypia).
EC5: - Lesions that are suspicious for borderline [OR] or malignant Phyllodes, [OR] DCIS (ductal carcinoma in situ), invasive mammary carcinoma, [OR] or encapsulated papillary carcinoma
EC6: - Any lesion that either the radiologist, pathologist [OR] or surgeon feels is [NOT] not amenable to VAPE [OR] or surgical excision
